headline: Reka AI has released a research preview of Rho-1, a single AI model that handles text, images, video and robot control.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an early research preview from a known lab with an unusual single-network design, but the report shows no results.
importance_line: Researchers and robotics teams get an early example of one model that takes in images, produces video and drives a robot, which The Decoder places in a wider push toward “world models” (AI that learns how the physical world works), but it is a research preview with no reported results.
summary: The Decoder reports that Reka AI, whose Reka Core model competed with GPT-4 and Claude 3 on benchmarks in April 2024, has released a research preview of Rho-1, one neural network that works with text, images, video and robot control actions at the same time, where most AI systems hand each kind of task to a separate specialist model. The same network that predicts camera images also drives robot movements; to get around the shortage of robot training data, Reka built a separate model that extracts control commands from ordinary internet videos, and the report gives no benchmark or robot test results.
notes: Full Decoder text read (fulltext HTTP 200); it is short, with no results and nothing on availability. Release date not stated; The Decoder published 5 Oct 2026 and MarkTechPost followed on 6 Oct 2026, and a 14-day search found no earlier coverage, so NEW.
